body:
From the named-bool check

Reviewed commit `0ee8671d355863658bbf292a12e04a566ac1af29` against merge base `82d05e94bea0dda172c9d23a7b5f58e90a7d7f49`. Rule applied (jhan, 2026-10-15): use a named `constexpr bool` only where a bool is passed as an argument in a function call or constructor call or template argument. The reason is, at a call site a bare `true` or `false` does not say what it means. Only lines added by this PR were checked.

No finding. The 20 lines this PR adds to `t/t_llama_unit.cpp`, the only changed file with a bool candidate, hold no bare `true` or `false` as an argument and no named literal bool outside an argument position. The one `constexpr bool` added there, `amx_qk_vnni_accepts`, is a computed `requires` expression. The other changed files have no `true`/`false` literal and no named bool constant on their added lines.

Not flagged: `return true;`, assignments, comparisons, variable initializers, designated initializers, bare literals in default arguments, Catch2 macros, and computed `constexpr bool` values (`std::is_same_v`, `requires`, trait specializations).

For reference: on `main`, the parameter-name comment form `/*name=*/true` appears 454 times and no `*_TRUE` / `*_FALSE` constant exists outside `numeric_limits` traits. The rule above was applied as written.

The no-finding result comes from one finder agent that listed every added line with a bool candidate and classified it; no code was built or run for this check.
